Hi Julia — great to meet (virtually) on Monday — confirming the 10:00 PT slot and sending a short pre-read and calendar invite.

High-level pre-read (bullets so your team can skim):
- Dedicated pools: we size by sustained QPS and token distribution. For your steady 550 QPS with 6–18 tokens, 3x the estimated worker count gives headroom for sustained load; for burst events we support burst capacity via autoscaling and short-lived burst nodes.
- Cold-starts & pre-warm: we recommend keeping a warm pool; runtime supports KV/prefix caching and an always-hot set of workers to keep p99 tails low. Typical p99 for your profile on our optimized kernels is ~100–140ms when warm; cold-start tails depend on node spin-up policy (we can configure fast-warm policies).
- Fallbacks & graceful degradation: policy-driven routing allows fallback to a quantized model variant or to an approximate mode (reduced context) to trade accuracy for latency. Queuing is bounded — requests may be queued briefly but we prefer model variant fallback for user-facing surfaces.
- Observability: token-level latencies, p99 across routes, trace links, and audit logs are available in Redwood Console.

Attachments: I've added a 1-page runbook (runbook-dedicated-fitcall.pdf) and linked the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234560/deal/CHR-2027-09-04

Call details: Mon Sep 6, 10:00 PT / 13:00 ET — Google Meet: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=chronosai-fitcall-20270906
Agenda (30 min):
- 5m intros & success criteria
- 10m traffic profile and sizing implications (we'll review your PDF)
- 10m runtime behavior + fallback policies
- 5m next steps (POC sizing / trial Dedicated pool)

If you want a short technical deep-dive instead of the high-level runbook, Irene can extend by 30m after the slot. Marcus (ops) is on to capture any procurement/portal questions for Dedicated.
